subject: gray wolf
title: Minnesota Wolves Wait Up to 30 Hours in Silence for One Beaver

scenes.text: Some wolves don't chase their dinner. They wait for it.
In Minnesota's Voyageurs National Park, wolves lie beside the trails beavers use to reach trees.
A typical stakeout lasts about four hours. Some last twelve. The longest recorded lasted thirty.
Most fail. Researchers found about 750 empty ambush beds for 214 beaver kills.
But from spring to autumn, beavers can make up 42 percent of a pack's diet.
In these woods, the most patient wolf eats best.

description:
Wolves in Voyageurs National Park, Minnesota, ambush beavers instead of chasing them.
The Voyageurs Wolf Project found stakeouts beside beaver trails average about 4 hours, often 8 to 12, and once 30 hours. Over five years researchers found 214 beaver kills and about 748 failed ambush sites, yet beavers made up as much as 42 percent of a pack's diet from April to October.
Would you have the patience of a wolf?
first_comment: Four hours is a normal wait for these wolves. How long could you sit perfectly still?
